headline: Committee recommends Bill 68 parking changes on first reading in 9-0 vote

meeting.body: Maui County Council Water and Infrastructure Committee
meeting.summary: The bill updates Park Maui rules, including two free hours for Hawaiʻi residents at the Wailuku Garage and paid parking zones at three Lahaina lots. It now goes to the full council.
meeting.recap: The committee's only item was Bill 68 (2026), which updates County parking rules for the Park Maui program.[[0:03:10]] Under the bill, Hawaiʻi residents who scan a valid Hawaiʻi driver's license at the Wailuku Garage get the first two hours free.[[0:07:08]] The bill removes a dirt area at Kamaʻole Beach 3 from resident-only beach hours, which the department said was listed by mistake.[[0:07:28]] Resident-only hours mean that on weekends and County holidays, parking at certain beaches is for residents only before 10 a.m.[[0:07:49]] The bill also creates paid parking zones at three lots in Lahaina.[[0:08:15]] No one signed up to give public testimony.[[0:09:52]] The department said the 500 Front Street lot may leave the Park Maui program in the future, but they don't know when.[[0:15:58]] A council member's question about whether that fee is allowed will be sent in writing to the County's lawyers.[[0:40:53]] A motion was made to recommend passing Bill 68 on first reading.[[0:44:30]] The motion passed with nine ayes and zero noes.[[0:47:44]] The bill now goes to the full council.[[0:47:53]]
meeting.next: Committee staff will send the question about the app convenience fee to the County's lawyers in writing.
